title: Death Penalty
rootClaim: The death penalty should be abolished globally as an irreversible, inhumane, and ineffective form of justice.

branches.text: Flaws in judicial procedures lead to the irreversible, state-sanctioned execution of innocent human beings.

children.text: DNA testing and post-conviction reviews have exonerated over 190 individuals from death row in the United States since 1973.
Systemic causes such as unreliable eyewitness testimony, coerced confessions, inadequate legal representation, and prosecutorial misconduct contaminate capital trials.

branches.text: Capital punishment violates the fundamental right to life and constitutes cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment.

children.text: Botched executions using untested lethal injection protocols cause intense prolonged suffering, violating constitutional protections against cruel and unusual punishment.

branches.text: Capital punishment is disproportionately applied based on race, socioeconomic status, and geographic jurisdiction rather than the severity of the crime.

children.text: Empirical studies consistently show that defendants accused of killing white victims face significantly higher probabilities of receiving a death sentence than those accused of killing minority victims.

branches.text: Capital punishment provides necessary moral proportionality and retributive justice for the most heinous offenses.

children.text: Retributivism maintains that the severity of punishment must match the moral gravity of the crime to uphold society's moral order.
State-sanctioned execution undermines the sanctity of life and reduces the justice system to institutionalized vengeance.

branches.text: The death penalty deters potential offenders from committing premeditated murder.

children.text: Criminological consensus and FBI homicide data demonstrate no statistically significant difference in murder rates between states with and without the death penalty.

definitions.description: A theory of justice asserting that criminals deserve to suffer punishment proportional to the severity of their wrongdoing.
The official absolution of a convicted person following clear evidence establishing their innocence.
An execution encounter that experiences breakdown, unnecessary delay, or severe suffering contrary to established legal standard protocols.
